# SCORE-VALUE-ALIGNMENT-01: what the committed panels can say about battery v3

**Status:** DEVELOPMENT analysis on committed public evidence. No model was trained, no solver was run, and no hidden bank or AX42 material was read. [The machine-readable audit](report.json) is generated by `python -m scripts.dev.battery.score_value_alignment_report`; it records the source SHA-256 for each row. Intervals below are deterministic 500-draw **descriptive** cluster bootstraps over recipes or families (seed 20261009), not qualification intervals. Shared decision scenarios and adaptive PRACTICE exposure are not independent draws.

## Answer to the owner's question

**We cannot yet tell whether v3 fixes the eight-member v2 inversion.** The eight Graphite members have v2 scores on 200 public PRACTICE cases and EV4 development decision values. Their recorded Kendall τ-b is **−0.473** and Spearman ρ is **−0.539**. The committed panel does not have any of the three *registered v3* measures for those same members: accuracy on v3 screening cases, mean regret on that batch's settled Q3 quiz, or the scoring-set false-feasible rate. V3 τ/ρ and every v3 term contribution are therefore **uncomputable**, not zero and not a failed result.

The owner-approved [v3 decision](../../../../.agent/decisions/2026-10-08-OWNER-BATTERY-SCORE-RULE-01.md) cites a separate sealed tuning study: its adopted candidate had τ 0.227 versus 0.146 for that study's deciding comparator. That is encouraging evidence **on its own tuning population**. It cannot be transferred to these eight Graphite members or treated as a held-out result. The tuning curves and per-member legs are not committed here.

## Strictly versioned measurements

All correlations use larger score against smaller decision loss. Run-5 has an exact common resolved scenario mask. EV4/EV5's historical `control-exam-v1` comparisons use their recorded per-member resolved loss, so they are context, not a matched v2/v3 experiment.

| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Graphite run-5 Q1 | v2 public PRACTICE | one seed / 8 | −0.473 | −0.539 | [−1.000, 0.341] | [−1.000, 0.530] |
| Graphite run-5 Q1 | v2 public PRACTICE | all three seeds / 27 | −0.107 | −0.107 | [−0.744, 0.393] | [−0.855, 0.535] |
| Run-5 Q1 refined references | v2 public PRACTICE | one seed / 8 | −0.473 | −0.539 | [−1.000, 0.341] | [−1.000, 0.530] |
| Run-5 Q1 refined references | v2 public PRACTICE | all three seeds / 27 | −0.080 | −0.080 | [−0.685, 0.363] | [−0.809, 0.507] |
| EV4 | `control-exam-v1`, **not v2** | development / 100 | 0.095 | 0.139 | [−0.031, 0.216] | [−0.052, 0.324] |
| EV4 | `control-exam-v1`, **not v2** | verification / 100 | 0.400 | 0.554 | [0.270, 0.517] | [0.383, 0.686] |
| EV5 | `control-exam-v1`, **not v2** | development / 100 | 0.126 | 0.195 | [−0.022, 0.262] | [−0.019, 0.386] |

The two EV panels recorded a different rule and a different model population, so their positive verification correlations neither repair nor contradict run-5's v2 result. The [quiz-design public stand-ins](../battery-quiz-designs/README.md) contain aggregate control curves, not matched per-member score and decision-value pairs; no τ/ρ for v2 or v3 can be extracted from those curves.

## Score terms and the six run-5 divergences

The v2 score in this Q1 study is the **single PRACTICE error** (lower is better). It rewards accuracy on those cases. The v3 rule is `sqrt(a × q)` for eligible members, where `a = 1/(1 + E)` on its registered screening cases and `q = 1/(1 + mean Q3 decision regret)` on its settled quiz. A scoring-set false-feasible rate above 0.05 makes a member ineligible and cannot be offset by either soft leg. These are the [VALIDATOR-26](../../../../.agent/tickets/VALIDATOR-26_battery_rule_v3.md) definitions. The v2 PRACTICE error, EV4 decision loss, EV4 near-limit plating false acceptance, and Q3 public stand-in control curves have different populations or meanings; substituting any of them for a v3 leg would change the rule or reuse the value outcome as an input to the score.

The six conditions below are **historical v2 accuracy-ordering divergences** on the one-seed panel. Every listed member scored above at least one better decider; the baseline MLP's PRACTICE error was 0.07405 and its decision loss was 0. Each member's proposed v3 flip term is **unknown**: the accuracy contribution, Q3 regret contribution, and G-FEAS verdict cannot be assigned from committed data.

| Graphite proposal (first seed) | v2 PRACTICE error | EV4 development decision loss | Term explaining historical ranking | v3 flip term |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| `p-1d4aaff5d292` | 0.05620 | 1.71874 | v2 accuracy error | unknown |
| `p-37985e699fe3` | 0.06305 | 1.68674 | v2 accuracy error | unknown |
| `p-4fd7fb870d2b` | 0.06051 | 1.69356 | v2 accuracy error | unknown |
| `p-69268f1b74ec` | 0.05944 | 0.02689 | v2 accuracy error | unknown |

| `p-c41a9a1ebb82` | 0.06136 | 1.69356 | v2 accuracy error | unknown |

The one-seed confidence band spans negative and positive alignment. The three-seed result moves toward zero, and its band also spans both signs. This is thin evidence even for the v2 population; no prospective score recommendation should rest on those eight members.

## Smallest evidence needed to answer the v3 question

For **each of the same eight member identities**, an operator-side, digest-bound table needs:

1. `a` measured on the specified v3 screening cases, with the exact rule and scoring-set identities;
2. `q` from predictions on the corresponding settled Q3 quiz and its registered regret/feasible-scenario rule, with missing candidate outcomes separated from missing references or infrastructure;
3. the per-case false-feasible rate on that scoring set, plus the G-FEAS verdict at 0.05;
4. the existing common-mask EV4 decision value bound to the member identity, and a genuinely held-out decision split declared before examining variant results.

Only an **operator-side aggregate report** needs to leave that environment. The 130 MB run-5 prediction bundles are not committed, and this ticket does not request or inspect them. Historical v2 scores remain historical; a v3 analysis would be a prospective counterfactual on the same model identities, not a rescore of their official records.

For a future held-out comparison, the following **already registered** candidates give three predeclared variants without selecting weights on this eight-member outcome: adopted `G-FEAS/A-Q@0.05`, `D|feas@0.05` (Q3 primary with the same gate), and `G-FEAS/A-Q@0.02` (the stricter gate in registry v4's sweep). Each candidate's held-out τ/ρ is **unavailable** until the above leg table and held-out values exist. The two alternatives are probes, not owner-approved rules or threshold recommendations. Retain the adopted v3 rule as the working prospective rule; make no claim yet that it fixes run-5's inversion.

**Reproduce:** `python -m scripts.dev.battery.score_value_alignment_report > /tmp/score-value-alignment.json` in a development checkout. The script reads only the committed Q1/EV JSON files and verifies their recorded historical τ (and Q1 ρ) before printing. [The JSON report](report.json) is the 500-draw output. No quiz-design aggregate is converted into member-level data.
